conventions.axes: Y-up, right-handed; camera looks down -Z by default; ground is the XZ plane at y = 0
conventions.lightIntensity: three.js physical units (directional/hemisphere/ambient: lux-like; spot/point: candela, decay 2)
conventions.easing: named functions from kit/time.js `ease` (formulas in references/kit-api.md)
conventions.camera: fov is vertical field of view in degrees (three.js convention); sensor-agnostic

style.name: Stained Glass
style.description: A cathedral leaded window seen from a dim stone nave: coloured glass panes (thickness variation, seeds/bubbles, ripple, darker edges at the lead) held in dark lead came with soldered joints and iron saddle bars, set in a splayed stone reveal; lit from behind, the window throws coloured light shafts through dusty air and coloured patches (lead lines and all) across the flagstones. An image is assembled pane by pane, the light comes up behind it, and each region glows as it is named while the sun moves.
motion: The lead came is laid first: every came grows along its edge (bottom up, frame first), soldered joints appear as the lines meet.
Panes are SET into the leading one by one: each flies in from the nave side, turns and settles flat into its cell (one glass tick per bin).
The light comes up behind the glass: the whole window glows, shafts appear in the dusty air, coloured patches land on the floor.
Each region glows brighter as it is named, then settles; the sun moves slowly so shafts and floor patches sweep.

objects.procedural: stone nave: 22 x 11 m ashlar wall at z = 0 with a pointed-arch hole, a splayed stone reveal down to the glass (z = -0.42), 22 x 22 m flagstone floor that receives the coloured window light
leaded stained-glass window: merged pane mesh (custom glass shader, per-pane flight into its cell), instanced lead came, solder joints, iron saddle bars
raymarched light-shaft volume (box) sampling the window light cookie along the sun direction; additive

scene.notes: The window plan (pane polygons, lead order, set times) is glazing.planGlazing(layoutWindow(DESIGN), GLAZE), computed identically in Node (SCORE) and the browser (picture). Floor patches and shafts are cookie lookups along the sun direction (SUN keys), not baked.
